chunks: And that which was narrated: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from al-Abbas from Mansur from Ali ibn Asbat from Sulayman ibn Abi Zaynab from Hariz from Zurara from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
"There is no harm if a man departs (from Mina) in the first departure before the sun passes its zenith."

This is applicable in a state of necessity; as for doing so by choice, then it is not permissible according to what we have mentioned. And whoever stays overnight on the second day until the sun sets, it is not permissible for him to depart to the third day, nor is it permissible for him to depart at night. He narrated.

key_terms.يَوْمَ الثَّانِي: The second day (11th of Dhu al-Hijjah)

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for leaving Mina early or late during Hajj?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Baqir (AS), transmitted via the chain of Zurarah, clarifies the jurisprudential distinction between voluntary and necessary early departure from Mina. It establishes that while the first Nafar is permissible before midday only under compulsion, those who extend their stay to the second day must wait until sunset to depart, prohibiting night travel to ensure order and reverence during the ritual. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on adhering to specific temporal markers in Hajj rites as derived from the Ahl al-Bayt.
